english.title: Fail to report a serious adverse event at a trial site immediately to the sponsor

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Medicines for Human Use Clinical Trials Regulations

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the investigator in relation to a clinical trial, failed to report a serious adverse event which occurred in a participant, namely **(..SPECIFY THE NAME OF THE SUBJECT..), at a trial site at which you were responsible for the conduct of the clinical trial immediately to the sponsor, namely **(..SPECIFY THE NAME OF THE SPONSOR..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 32(1), 49(1)(g) and 52 of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Regulation 51 of the of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004 provides a defence of due diligence.
(ii) This offence applies from the 28th April 2026 due to changes made by the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) (Amendment) Regulations 2025. For the offence applicable before this date, see H15920.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 3 months imprisonment and / or a fine
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
